rule: Allow Node assert candidates only when they verify machine-consumed sentinels, parser fixtures, shipped source-to-artifact equality, required machine-field presence, or observable routing, lifecycle, transformation, and deduplication behavior without pinning free-standing authored prose.

allowed.rationale: Verifies that idle events from unrelated or merely lineage-connected fixture sessions do not invoke prompt or promptAsync; promptCalls.length is an observable lifecycle side effect, and the synthetic session IDs are not production identifiers being pinned.
Verifies exactly one continuation injection for an explicitly tracked boulder session; this is dispatch and lifecycle behavior independent of continuation wording or fixture session-ID spelling.
Checks the native-skill registry invariant that each source equals join(nativeSkillsRoot, name); the resulting path is consumed by synchronization code and no SKILL prose is inspected.
Verifies that the onboarding registry entry resolves to its executable filesystem source under the native-skills root; this is package synchronization routing rather than authored onboarding content.

Uses synthetic markdown input to prove the compatibility transformer is a no-op when no OpenCode orchestration-call syntax is present; the equality covers input/output transformation behavior, not shipped prose.
allowed.expected: --- name: test --- # Test Skill No orchestration here.

allowed.rationale: Checks presence of the exact compatibility-section marker consumed by insertion, removal, and duplicate-detection code after transformation; it does not independently contract the surrounding guidance prose.
Pins the compatibility heading only as the section identity marker mechanically consumed by the transformer for insertion, removal, and deduplication, not as free-standing SKILL wording.
Verifies that parsed YAML frontmatter remains at the start when generated compatibility guidance is inserted; this protects markdown transformation structure rather than guidance wording.

Verifies that generated compatibility guidance precedes the first incompatible orchestration example, including after stale-section repair; this is required insertion and repair behavior rather than editorial section ordering.

Compares transformed output with the same dynamic input fixture to prove idempotent no-op behavior when an existing compatibility section is already correctly positioned; this is not shipped-copy equality or a separate authored fragment.
Verifies that content without frontmatter gets the generated compatibility section prepended; the seam is transformer placement using the production-consumed section marker.
Checks that no-frontmatter input begins with the generated compatibility section; the exact value is the transformer's machine-consumed marker and the behavior under test is placement at offset zero.
Confirms that original synthetic fixture content survives prepend transformation; the Test Skill heading is fixture payload and is not required in production SKILL copy.
Checks preservation of a synthetic markdown fixture fragment after prepend transformation; it does not require a shipped skill to contain this heading.

Checks the sentence-shaped suffix as a production parser sentinel in senpiCompatibilityEndMarkers, where it is consumed to recognize generated guidance and locate section boundaries rather than merely pinning prose.

Uses the production-consumed compatibility-section marker to derive occurrence count after stale-section repair; the regex supports marker-based deduplication rather than an unparsed heading contract.
Verifies deduplication behavior: stale compatibility guidance is removed and exactly one generated section remains after reprocessing.
Compares staged directive.md bytes with source directive bytes, so it remains valid across editorial rewrites and fails only when the packaged runtime copy diverges from its source.
